title: Morton's stories of the road and W. C. Handy's band
summary: Carew tells Morton's tales about the grip full of money and Handy's trouble leading a band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: may have been an out-of-town band jelly told me a couple of things about being on the road and romax wrote and asked me if i knew anything about his travels i said well only a couple of incidents which which are unimportant although they're kind of amusing jelly said that he used to collect for the for the dates and he put his money in in a grip he'd collect the cash at the end of the performance of the date and collect the cash from the uh the theater manager and count it put it in this grip and he says he carried around a while and he called one of the musicians one day that says him he says i'm going to make you custodian of this grip of mine he says i got other things to carry he says other things keep me busy he says i'll just make you custodian of that grip now he said don't let get out of your hands so the fellow says all right he didn't tell him what was in it so he said they went on several weeks so several dates at least so it came to time to get to a place where the he wanted to deposit he said he deposited in the bank he said so he took the fellow took the fellow down to the bank and said bring the bank bring that grip with you so he went down the bank he put it on the counter there and opened it up he said the other thing was loaded with money he said the fellow almost dropped dead did he keep carrying that much money around so he told me that little tale and he also told you know he had a date with handy one time he and handy a band in chicago played there at one time and he told me about handy he says handy was carrying on an affair with one of the players one of the players wives and he says uh somebody told handy that the fellow was wise to him and he says he says whenever handy tried to lead after that he said he always had to keep one eye on this man he said why don't you try to lead the band yet watch that
fellow all the time that wasn't a very uh long lasting band and uh this man had something to do with it
handy handy wrote a letter to me and said he says my own band he said and i couldn't even lead it he said he
